tasks.short: Talk with colleagues and counsellors about a student's problem, share information and follow up by e-mail and phone, look up earlier incidents and agreements, and note new agreements in the student's file.

steps.what: Residential advisor communicates with other staff to resolve problems with individual students
Residential advisor shares information with staff and follows up: by e-mail and phone today, by notes and tasks in the student's case after the change
Residential advisor looks up the student's earlier incidents and agreements
Residential advisor notes agreements: in the student's file today, in the student's case after the change

tasks.design: Each student with a problem gets a case in the residence system ({OTHER}) with earlier incidents, agreements and follow-up tasks visible to the staff involved, so information is not passed by e-mail chains and tasks do not get lost. Access is limited to staff who need it. Talking with colleagues and deciding what to do stay with the advisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information sat in e-mails and notebooks of different staff.
tasks.enabler_now: Residence systems hold student cases with tasks and access rights.
tasks.still_hard: Staff work different shifts and miss each other.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the pattern behind a student's repeated small problems.

reach.learn: Whether cases are handed over complete.

evidence.claim: Residence systems can hold student cases with follow-up tasks and access rights.
Notes on students' health are special category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student problem to agreements noted; counselling is outside.
Input contract: incidents and agreements kept in the residence system; fallback is e-mail and notebooks.

Talks with colleagues and noting agreements keep their full time. s2 keeps 70 because the information is still written; only forwarding mails and chasing status go. s3 keeps 40 because earlier incidents and agreements are in the case; older ones still sit in notebooks.
Colleagues use the case as they would e-mail.
research_questions: Do follow-up tasks get done more often?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: colleagues keep using e-mail and much history is still in notebooks (6.5); high: staff work in the case and history is there (16.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe students in the hall, decide whether behavior is unusual and write an incident report, send it to the residence manager, and talk with the student or counsellor about serious cases.

steps.what: Residential advisor observes students to detect unusual behavior
Residential advisor decides whether the behavior seen is unusual
Residential advisor writes an incident report with type, place and what happened
Residential advisor checks the final incident report: type, place and what happened as seen, and that it goes to the residence manager
Residential advisor submits the checked report to the residence manager: by e-mail today, from the phone form after the change
Residential advisor talks with the student or counsellor about serious cases

tasks.design: Incident reports are a short form on the advisor's phone in the residence system ({OTHER}) with type, place and what happened; the advisor writes what happened, checks the report and submits it to the residence manager. Observing students and judging what is unusual stay with the advisor; no camera or software analyses students' behavior.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports were typed at the end of the shift and e-mailed.
tasks.enabler_now: Phone incident forms are common in residence systems.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a student who stopped coming to the shared kitchen.

reach.learn: Whether reports arrive the same night.

evidence.claim: Residence systems offer phone incident forms that route to a manager.
Apps that time-stamp each staff action can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from residents to the case followed up; disciplinary decisions are outside.
Input contract: report form set by the residence office; fallback is typed reports.

Observing, judging, checking the report and talking with students keep their full time. s3 keeps 85 because only type and place become picks; the advisor still writes what happened. s4 keeps 25 for the submit.
research_questions: Do managers act on incidents sooner?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: the residence office sets the form, and learning it is a one-off.

approvals.approved_version: The incident report exactly as checked by the advisor in s3c, submitted once to the residence manager in the residence system; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: advisors still type full reports at the end of the shift, so only the e-mail step changes (3.0); high: reports are written on the phone form (4.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Make the duty roster, supervise and coach residence hall staff, train new resident assistants, write evaluations, sign them, send them to the housing office, and approve student workers' hours.

steps.what: Resident assistants enter their availability in the scheduling tool
Residential advisor makes the duty roster: in a spreadsheet today; after the change the tool proposes it from availability and rules and the advisor adjusts it
Residential advisor checks the final roster: every duty covered, rest times kept and a fair spread of night duties
Residential advisor publishes the checked roster to the staff
Residential advisor supervises residence hall staff and student workers
Residential advisor trains new resident assistants
Residential advisor evaluates the work of each staff member and student worker
Student workers enter the hours they actually worked in the scheduling tool
Residential advisor writes evaluations of staff and student workers: on a paper form today, on the HR system's form after the change
Residential advisor checks and signs the evaluations
The signed evaluations are filed: e-mailed to the housing office today, filed in the HR system after the change
Residential advisor checks student workers' hours against the roster and known absences: on paper timesheets today, in the scheduling tool after the change
Residential advisor releases the checked hours to payroll: by handing in timesheets today, by one release in the tool after the change

tasks.design: Resident assistants enter their availability in a scheduling tool ({CALENDAR}) that proposes the duty roster within set rules; the advisor adjusts it, checks it and publishes it. Student workers enter the hours they actually worked; the advisor checks them against the roster and known absences and releases them to payroll ({PAYROLL}). Policy and safety modules for new assistants move to the learning system ({LMS}), so training time goes to practice. Evaluation forms in the HR system ({HCM}) are written by the advisor and, once signed, filed there. Supervising and coaching stay with the advisor; roster data are not used to rate staff without works council consent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rosters were built in spreadsheets, timesheets were paper and policies taught in person.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling tools, learning systems and HR forms are standard in universities.
tasks.still_hard: Student workers' availability changes with exams.
tasks.human_edge: Coaching a new assistant after a hard night on duty.

reach.learn: Whether rosters are fairer and more stable.

evidence.claim: Scheduling tools build rosters from availability; learning systems deliver policy modules.
Apps that time-stamp each staff action can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from staff availability to hours approved; hiring is outside.
Input contract: availability from assistants; policy modules from the housing office; fallback is spreadsheets and paper.

Supervising, coaching, judging, signing, checking the roster and checking hours keep their full time. s1 keeps 40 because the advisor still adjusts the proposed roster. s3 keeps 80 because only policy theory moves to modules. s5 keeps 90 because the advisor still writes each evaluation. s8r keeps 10 for the release.
Assistants enter availability (s0) and student workers enter their hours (s8h), share 1 each, in about the time a message or paper sheet took; this is outside the advisor's savings.

incremental.description: Residential advisor keeps roster rules and modules current.

approvals.approved_version: The evaluations exactly as checked and signed by the advisor in s6, filed once in each staff member's record in the HR system ({HCM}); any change needs a new check and signature.
The duty roster exactly as checked by the advisor in s1c, published once to the hall's staff in the scheduling tool; any change needs a new check.
Each student worker's hours for the pay period exactly as checked by the advisor in s8, released once to {PAYROLL}; any correction needs a new check and release.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small team whose roster hardly changes and few new assistants (10.4); high: many student workers with changing availability (17.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Walk regular rounds through the halls, record findings in the logbook, and report defects to facilities.

steps.what: Residential advisor makes regular rounds to ensure residents and areas are safe and secure
Residential advisor records round findings: in the logbook today, in a phone form with pick lists after the change
Residential advisor writes up each defect with a photo: by phone or e-mail today, as a ticket from the round form after the change
Residential advisor checks the final ticket: place, defect and urgency, and that the photo shows the defect and no residents
Residential advisor submits the checked ticket to the facilities desk

tasks.design: Round findings go into a phone form with pick lists, and a defect seen on the round becomes a ticket for the facilities desk ({HELPDESK}) from the same form with a photo; the advisor checks each ticket and submits it. Walking the rounds and judging what is unsafe stay with the advisor. The form logs findings, not the advisor's route or times, unless the works council agrees.
tasks.previous_blocker: Findings were written in a paper logbook and defects reported by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Phone forms and facilities ticket desks are common.
tasks.still_hard: Safety issues at night need action, not a ticket.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing that a quiet corridor is too quiet.

reach.learn: Whether defects come with photos and places.

evidence.claim: Phone forms can log round findings and open facilities tickets with photos.
Apps that time-stamp each staff action can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the round schedule to defects reported; repairs are outside.
Input contract: facilities desk takes tickets; fallback is the logbook and phone.

Walking rounds, checking and submitting tickets keep their full time. s2 keeps 90 because the advisor still records each finding; only date, time and place are filled. s3 keeps 50 because the finding is not retyped into an e-mail or told by phone; the photo and details stay.

incremental.description: Residential advisor checks open tickets on the next round.

approvals.approved_version: The ticket with place, defect, urgency and photo exactly as checked by the advisor in s3c, submitted once to the facilities desk queue ({HELPDESK}); any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: urgent defects are still phoned through, so most reports are told twice (2.1); high: defects go as tickets from the form (4.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The residential advisor keeps talking with staff and students, observing, supervising and walking rounds; e-mail chains, paper logbooks and spreadsheet rosters shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An advisor with more time among residents.
